public_rationale: On the plain reading, 'movies' means feature films made mainly with Sora. No such film was released. On March 24, 2026, OpenAI announced it was shutting down Sora. Its developer notice set September 24, 2026 for removing all Sora 2 models and the Videos API, with no replacement. The app went dark on April 26. The best-known feature built partly with Sora, Critterz, missed its planned Cannes 2026 premiere because Sora was withdrawn. It was described as 'human-led but AI-assisted' in any case. Since Sora was discontinued before generating any feature film, the forecast is settled early as supported. One caveat: TechCrunch said on the day of the announcement that the model was still reachable inside ChatGPT.
limitations: The early resolution depends on Sora's discontinuation. It is not confirmed whether access inside ChatGPT also ended.
A film using Sora footage made before the shutdown could still be released. It would count against the claim only if Sora generated most of it.
Under a broader reading of 'movies' that includes curated short films, the result could differ.

statement.excerpt: Sora is not going to generate movies.

from_speaker: Sora is not going to generate movies
It's going to continue making horrifying human-adjacent creatures
cartoons that look remarkably like copyrighted material
our_interpretation: Plain reading of 'movies': feature-length films generated mainly by Sora and released publicly. Short clips, short films cut by humans from curated Sora clips, and human-led films that use Sora as one tool among many do not count. In context he was dismissing claims that Sora would replace film-making.
No deadline was stated, so the forecast is open-ended unless a decisive event settles it.
criteria.support_condition: Sora stops being available for generation before any feature-length film made mainly with Sora is publicly released.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A feature-length film generated mainly with Sora is publicly released.
